title: Spike: programmatic lib/tasklist-rebuild.mjs API
description:
Architect-reviewer flagged ARCH-N-016-4: the existence of tests/fixtures/silent-loop-regression/fake-rebuild.mjs in test fixtures is a smell suggesting orchestrator could expose its own programmatic rebuild API. Currently rebuilds shell out to `npx tasklist-rebuild` from a sibling package (gen-tasklist plugin) — adds a runtime npm dependency, requires `rebuildCmd` config in fixtures, and prevents in-process testing.

This is a SPIKE to evaluate the design. Outputs:
1. Survey: what does `npx tasklist-rebuild` actually do? (Walk the gen-tasklist source.)
2. Boundary question: should orchestrator OWN rebuild, or remain a CONSUMER of gen-tasklist? (The lib boundary in the orchestrator project is small surface; gen-tasklist is the canonical home.)
3. Hybrid option: lightweight in-process rebuild for tests + production still uses npx (tests get fast hermetic rebuild, production gets battle-tested gen-tasklist)
4. Decision doc: ADR-style write-up with recommendation; if 'do it' then file follow-up implementation task.

Security callout: any new programmatic rebuild API must use writeJsonAtomic (TOCTOU candidate per security-auditor flag), enforce validateShardId on caller-supplied IDs even though current call sites use fs.readdirSync output.
acceptance_criteria: Decision doc at docs/adr/ADR-NNN-tasklist-rebuild-boundary.md (or similar) with: problem statement, options surveyed, trade-offs, recommendation
Recommendation is one of: (a) extract programmatic API to lib/, (b) keep npx-only and document, (c) hybrid (in-process for tests, npx for production)
If recommendation is (a) or (c), follow-up implementation task is filed with concrete acceptance criteria
